issues.body:
When the timed jena leg succeeds (j == s, so count_agree is True) but the entity-ID sidecar fails, the `rm -f "$TMP/jena-$wl.ids"` at line 301 makes read_ids return None, so ids_agree is False and the else-branch at line 439 fires. The envelope's timing cell then reads:

  WITHHELD(entity-list-disagree: counts=10, sparq-rows=10 jena-rows=0, |sparq\jena|=10 |jena\sparq|=0)

That string states as fact that jena returned an entirely disjoint entity set. What actually happened is that the oracle replay never produced an answer — a harness failure, not a result. This matters because the whole point of the envelope is that a disagreement IS a recorded result: a reader triaging this row would go looking for a jena k-NN correctness bug that does not exist.

The information needed to disambiguate is present but only elsewhere: count_crosscheck records jena_entity_ids as "n/a", and the log line at 300 says the oracle FAILED. Withholding the timing is the right call either way, so this is a labelling defect, not a soundness one. The symmetric case (sparq oracle absent, sparq-rows=0) has the same problem.
issues.title: A failed/absent jena oracle is reported as "entity-list-disagree", which asserts an engine disagreement that was never observed

issues.body:
The block at line 227 is guarded only by `[ "$SPARQ_STATUS" = "ok" ]`, not by `want jena-geosparql`. With ONLY=sparq (the GEO_SMOKE acceptance path) the two `nearest-ids` invocations still run, each re-reading the ~100k-triple corpus and rebuilding the GeoIndex from scratch, and the resulting .ids files are then never consumed — "jena-geosparql" is absent from engines_meta, so the timing block that reads them at line 428 is skipped entirely.

Pure waste rather than incorrectness, but it is added to the fastest acceptance path in the script.
issues.fix_hint: Add the existing helper to the guard: `if [ "$SPARQ_STATUS" = "ok" ] && want jena-geosparql; then`. The crosscheck is only meaningful when there is a competitor to cross-check against.
issues.title: sparq nearest-ids oracle runs even when jena-geosparql is not in ONLY, costing two extra 100k corpus load+index passes

issues.body:
Line 228 pins `"nearest_k10 10" "nearest_k100 100"` while the envelope derives k generically via `int(w.removeprefix("nearest_k"))` at line 406 and the jena side dispatches on the generic `[[ "$wl" == nearest_k* ]]`. Adding, say, nearest_k1000 to WORKLOADS (line 115) would produce a jena .ids file but no sparq one, giving sparq_ids=None -> ids_agree=False -> a permanently withheld timing plus the misleading "entity-list-disagree" string from the issue above.

Fail-closed, so nothing dishonest ships — but it fails silently, in the one direction a maintainer would not think to check.
issues.fix_hint:
Derive the list from WORKLOADS instead of restating it, e.g.

  for wl in $WORKLOADS; do
    [[ "$wl" == nearest_k* ]] || continue
    k="${wl#nearest_k}"
    ...
  done

which mirrors the generic dispatch the other two call sites already use.
issues.title: The oracle's (workload, k) pairs are hardcoded separately from WORKLOADS, so a future nearest_k workload silently loses its timing

issues.body:
The round-1 numbering fix is correct as far as it goes — "Two modes:" became "Modes:", nearest-ids got a Mode 3 heading, and query moved to Mode 4. But the fenced sh block at lines 6-14 still stops at #3, so `query <corpus.nt> <query.rq> [iters]` has a `## Mode 4` prose section with no corresponding entry in the usage block a reader scans first. (The default report mode dispatched at line 113 is listed as #1, so the block is otherwise complete.)

Pre-existing in spirit — query was equally missing when it was Mode 3 — but this PR is the one that touched the block.
issues.title: The fenced usage block lists 3 invocations but the file documents 4 modes; `query` is still absent from it

verdict.summary:
Round 2 fixes every round-1 finding, and I verified each independently rather than taking the diff's word for it.

Major 1 (unguarded sparq nearest-ids under set -e): now `if ! timeout "$TIMEOUT_S" ... ; then log; rm -f; fi` at scripts/bench/geo-same-box.sh:227-236 — matches the graceful-degradation contract of every other engine leg, and the `rm -f` makes the truncated-by-redirect file take the fail-closed path.

Major 2 (unbounded jena replay): now double-capped — outer `timeout "$TIMEOUT_S"` plus `urlopen(request, timeout=int(os.environ["TIMEOUT_S"]))`, with TIMEOUT_S exported into the sidecar env (line 280-292).

Minor 3 (WITHHELD string): count-disagree and entity-disagree are now distinct reasons, the latter carrying both row counts and the symmetric-difference sizes (line 437-454).

Minor 4 (design record): research/gap-geo-2026-07.md §3 and §5 both updated; §5's rendering corrected to spatialF:greatCircleGeom. I grepped the repo for surviving "only result-set SIZE" claims about nearest_k and found none — line 796's counts-only note belongs to the Geographica family, which has no nearest_k workload.

Minor 5 (cardinality): `len(sparq_ids) == expected_k and len(set(sparq_ids)) == expected_k` closes both the empty-set and duplicate-row holes.

Nit 6: "Modes:", a Mode 3 heading, and query renumbered to Mode 4.

Verification I ran: `cargo check -q -p sparq-geo --example bench_geo` clean; `bash -n` clean; I executed the new ids_agree expression standalone against both-None, [] == [], all-duplicates, jena-oracle-missing, and the good case — all fail closed (only the good case yields agree=True), and the conditional-expression precedence parses as intended. The sparq oracle calls the same `index.nearest(QUERY_CENTER, k)` that bench_mode times (bench_geo.rs:251-254 vs 137-141), and `<%s>` on the jena side matches oxrdf's NamedNode Display, so the two sides are format-compatible.

What remains is one reporting-clarity minor and three nits — no blocker or major.
